served.stem: 3,3-Dimethyl-1-butene is treated with HBr. Which structure is the major product? (Consider carbocation stability carefully.)
served.bankWhy: Markovnikov protonation gives a secondary cation at C2 next to the quaternary carbon; a 1,2-methyl shift gives a more stable tertiary cation that Br- traps, yielding 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane (keyed option A, canonical CC(C)C(C)(C)Br). The classic trap (option B) is the unrearranged secondary bromide.

answer.line: H+ makes a secondary cation next to a carbon holding three methyls. One methyl slides over, the cation turns tertiary, and bromide adds there.

steps: Protonate the alkene the Markovnikov way: H+ goes to the CH2 end and the plus sits on C2, a secondary carbon.
Look next door. C3 holds three methyls and no H, so a methyl slides over with its bond pair, and the plus moves to C3, now tertiary.
Bromide adds to the tertiary carbon: 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane. Some unshifted bromide forms too, but the shifted one is the major product.

choices.note: The skeleton did rearrange. But Br sits on a primary end carbon, not on the tertiary carbon that holds the charge.
Br on the end carbon is anti-Markovnikov, the radical result of HBr with peroxides. There is no peroxide here.
This puts Br on one of the tert-butyl methyls. No cation ever forms on that carbon, so bromide has no way to reach it.
Methyl shift to the tertiary cation, then bromide.
This Markovnikov bromide forms too, from bromide catching the secondary cation first. The methyl shift to the tertiary cation is the move the item tests.
